terms.comment: lūdī scaenicī, plays, as against the games of the circus; poēta scaenicus, a dramatist; as a noun scaenicus is an actor (Cic. Off. 1.114).

evidence: Cic. Sest. 115: theātrālēs gladiātōriīque cōnsessūs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of the theatre and its audience rather than of plays; Quintilian’s theātrālis hūmānitās is put on for show (Quint. 2.2.10).

evidence: Diom. p. 480 P.: drāmaticum poēma (Lewis & Short, s.v. drāma)
terms.comment: A grammarian’s term for poetry in which the characters speak.
A plain description: the stage art, as artificēs scaenicī are actors (Cic. Arch. 10; Lewis & Short, s.v. scaenicus).

phrases.latin: hīs ego tamen diēbus lūdīs scaenicīs … dīrūpī mē paene in jūdiciō
phrases.english: yet these days, during the plays, I nearly burst myself in a trial

phrases.latin: nē scaenicī plūs quam nōs videantur habēre prūdentiae
phrases.english: so that actors may not seem to have more sense than we have
